summary: Phra Sigambhirayan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BLA from Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and an MA from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University. He served as an associate professor at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, attested in 2013.
Phramaha Niras Ruangsan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Sydney, supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.
Phramaha Sakda Hemthep is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MPhil at Cardiff University by 2014, supervised by Max Deeg.
Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Sydney under doctoral supervisor Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, attested in 2009.
Phrapongsak K. is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts in 2015 as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center.

Phuntsok Tashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a BA at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, an MA at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff is an Indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at Radcliffe College and Harvard University (PhD ~1973), she served as professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and Lex Hixon Professor of World Religions at Yale University (2004).

Pierce Salguero is a historian and scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his BA and MA at the University of Virginia and a PhD from Johns Hopkins University (~2010), becoming professor of Asian History and Health Humanities at Penn State Abington (~2010).

Pierre Bourdieu was a French sociologist and philosopher. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure and under Émile Benveniste, he held academic appointments at Lille, the École des hautes études en sciences sociales (1975), and the Collège de France (1981–2001).
Pierre Chantraine was a French linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes between ~1920 and ~1927. He later served as a professor at the University of Paris from ~1938 to ~1969.

Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat was an Indologist and linguist. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1967–2004), worked at the EFEO and EHESS, and served as President of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (2010).
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen is a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his PhD from Leiden University by 1991, where he was also attested as a research fellow in 1996.

Pieter Hendrik Pott was a Dutch scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as curator at the National Museum of Ethnology in Leiden (~1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.

Pietro Merlo was an Italian linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia and Giovanni Maria Bertini. From 1877 he taught at the University of Pavia, becoming full professor of comparative linguistics in 1885.

Piotr Balcerowicz is a Polish Indologist and philosopher educated at Warsaw, Banaras Hindu, Hamburg, and the Polish Academy of Sciences. He became a professor of Indology at the University of Warsaw and has held several international visiting professorships.

Piotr Klafkowski was a Polish scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He earned his PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań under Jerzy Bańczerowski and received instruction from Lozang Jamspal, Geleg Gyatso, and Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.

Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé was a Tibetan Buddhist scholar and master. He studied under Ngawang Palzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and his students included Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche and Chagdud Tulku Rinpoche.

Poerbatjaraka was an Indonesian scholar of linguistics, Indology, and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University under N. J. Krom and served as a professor at Gadjah Mada, University of Indonesia, and Udayana University, which he founded.

Polly Young-Eisendrath is a psychologist and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Ohio University, Goddard College, and Washington University in St. Louis (PhD ~1980). In 1994, she was appointed clinical associate professor in psychiatry at the University of Vermont.
Pori Park is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. She has served as an assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.
